stem: Over what timeframe should a gastroenteritis-related fluid deficit be replaced in a child?
explanation: Over 24 to 48 hours is the standard timeframe for replacing a gastroenteritis-related fluid deficit in a child.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the fluid deficit in gastroenteritis is replaced gradually over 24 to 48 hours.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because this is too rapid for standard deficit replacement.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because this is still faster than the usual 24 to 48 hour replacement window.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because deficit replacement is part of the overall fluid management plan and is not deferred until maintenance fluids are finished.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because this is far longer than the recommended replacement period.
